author: Linnaeus, 1758
habitat: 호수와 하천의 물가, 갈대밭, 배 밭
summary: 흔하지 않은 나그네새로, 이동할 때 제비 무리에 섞여 다니며 배 밭이나 갈대밭을 잠자리로 삼는다. 물 위를 나는 곤충 따위를 날면서 잡아먹는다. 호수와 하천 물가의 모래땅이나 흙 벼랑, 밭의 모래층에 굴을 파 많은 수가 모여 번식하며, 6~7월에 한배에 3~5개의 알을 낳는다. 시베리아 남동부, 아무르, 사할린, 쿠릴 열도, 홋카이도에서 번식한다.

points.en: black bill and dark brown legs

art.subject: Sand Martin (Riparia riparia), adult on migration (May and August–September): forehead, crown, nape, lores, ear-coverts and cheeks plain dark earth-brown; chin and throat white, the white curving up behind the ear-coverts as a half-collar; a clear-cut dark brown band across the breast; belly, flanks and undertail coverts white; back, scapulars, rump and uppertail coverts the same dark earth-brown as the crown, with no pale rump; wings and short tail dark brown; underwing dark grey-brown; tiny black bill; dark eye; dark brown legs.
art.pose: in flight low over water, hawking insects
art.scene: Korean lake shore with open water and reedbeds during migration; no people, buildings or text
views: adult, side view perched on a reed stem: dark earth-brown head and upperparts, brown ear-coverts, white throat curving up behind them, clear dark brown breast band, white belly, wingtips reaching beyond the short notched tail, tiny black bill, dark legs
adult, in flight seen from below: white throat, distinct brown breast band, white belly and undertail coverts, dark grey-brown underwings, short shallowly notched tail, head, body and tail in line
art.build: Small, slim swallow, clearly smaller than a Barn Swallow and without tail streamers. Head rounded, with a tiny, short, flat black bill and a wide gape. Legs very short, dark brown, seen only when it perches on wires or reeds. Wings long, narrow and pointed; at rest the wingtips extend beyond the tail tip. Tail short with only a shallow notch. Flight fluttery and erratic, low over water, often in flocks mixed with Barn Swallows; from below the brown breast band separates the white throat from the white belly.
avoid: Do not leave out the brown breast band; it is this species' key mark (Pale Martin, Riparia diluta, has only a faint, diffuse band).
Do not paint glossy blue upperparts, a red throat or long tail streamers — those are Barn Swallow traits.
Do not paint a white or rufous rump (Asian House Martin, Red-rumped Swallow); the rump is brown like the back.
Do not make the tail deeply forked.
